title: Gearbox endurance rig
description: Endurance test rig for heavy-duty truck gearboxes. The input is driven by a 400 kW electric motor at up to 2,500 rpm and the output is loaded by an absorber. Gearbox oil is conditioned to 120 °C. Between runs, technicians swap the gearbox using the hall crane. The rig is run from a PLC with an HMI, and the supplier asks for remote diagnostics.

title: Hydraulic hose pulse bench
description: Pressure pulse bench for hydraulic hoses up to 600 bar, fed by a hydraulic power unit with a bladder accumulator. Hoses are fitted by hand inside a test chamber with an interlocked door. Test fluid is heated to 100 °C. The pulse sequence is programmed on the bench controller.

title: Diesel injector test bench
description: Bench for functional testing of diesel injectors. Injectors are mounted manually and spray calibration fluid into a measuring chamber; the high-pressure pump is belt-driven by an electric motor. Results are stored locally.

title: Battery module handling cell
description: Automated cell where an industrial robot moves battery modules between a conveyor and test fixtures. Staff place pallets at a load port. The cell runs on a safety PLC and is connected to the plant MES for test orders.

title: Walk-in climate chamber
description: Walk-in climate chamber from -40 to +85 °C for cab components, with a compressor refrigeration circuit. Personnel walk in to place test objects. A programmable controller runs the temperature profiles.

title: Cab door durability rig
description: Durability rig that opens and slams a cab door 200,000 times using cylinders on 6 bar shop air. A light curtain protects the area where the door is set up. Simple relay logic, no network connection.

title: Chassis dyno control upgrade
description: Upgrade of the existing chassis dynamometer controls: new PLC program, new HMI, and a support connection so the supplier can troubleshoot from their office. No mechanical changes.

title: Brake dynamometer
description: Brake dynamometer for drum and disc brakes with flywheel inertia up to 2,000 kg·m². Brake temperatures reach 700 °C and dust is extracted. Brake assemblies are lifted into place with a jib crane.
